note: Section 14: real generation-throughput impact of live KV movement, SmolLM2-135M, Vulkan, 32 generated tokens, transfer_every_n=8 for scenarios C/D. All four scenarios run on the SAME prompt/model, back to back. Raw data: raw_decode_impact_135m.jsonl (ctx=2048), raw_decode_impact_135m_ctx16384.jsonl (ctx=16384).

scenarios.A_no_transfers: pure baseline, no movement at all
scenarios.B_one_transfer_before_generation: one single-layer (K+V) round trip immediately before the generation loop starts
scenarios.C_periodic_single_layer_every_8_tokens: one single-layer (K+V) round trip every 8 generated tokens (4 total over 32 tokens)
scenarios.D_worst_case_all_layers_every_8_tokens: ALL layers' K+V round-tripped every 8 generated tokens (4 total) -- the deliberately pessimistic synchronous case

note_on_A_vs_B_C_apparent_speedup: scenarios B/C show slightly HIGHER tok/s than A in these measurements -- this is run-to-run noise/warmup effects on a small, fast model (each scenario reloads the model fresh), not a genuine benefit from transferring data; the meaningful signal here is scenario D's clear, large cost, not small differences between A/B/C which are within measurement noise (compare to performance.json's own noise-disclosure precedent from Phase 11E).
finding: single-layer, targeted movement (scenarios B and C) is cheap at every tested context -- under 3.5% stall even at ctx=16384, negligible at ctx=2048. The DELIBERATELY worst-case scenario (D: all 30 layers' K+V, synchronously, every 8 tokens) is genuinely expensive: 7.5% stall at ctx=2048, but 47% stall and roughly HALVED generation throughput at ctx=16384 -- transfer cost scales with KV size while compute-per-token does not, so the worst case gets proportionally worse at larger contexts. This directly supports Section 15/23's conclusion: naive, frequent, whole-cache synchronous movement is impractical at scale, but the STATIC, load-time-only tiering mechanism this phase's core VRAM-reduction results (vram_reduction.json, second_model.json, pressure_test.json) actually rely on requires ZERO runtime transfer cost at all -- it is decided once, before generation starts, not repeated per token.
